translations.text: deceiving herself and crowds of senseless people, like animals with no knowledge of the Scriptures.
Only because of pride, as I said before,
and disobedience, all these crowds are going down to Hades, whether male or female. For it is because of pride and disobedience, as we said before.
that the devil was thrown out of heaven at the beginning.
Who, then, can count those who have perished from the beginning, going down into the pit,
because they walked on the path of pride and lived in [?] disobedience?
For after everything the Lord said from the beginning, whether in parables or in plain language, the last of all the things he said was:
“Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.” Does not everyone have ears? Or has a human being ever existed without ears?
Does the creator of everything, the King, Christ, not know that he has never created a person without ears?
And what is this saying that he spoke: “Let anyone who has ears listen”?
But because he knows that pride in people is an abomination before God, as he said,
he therefore said, “Let anyone who has ears to hear listen,” because of disobedience
and pride, about which Scripture said, “My people did not listen to my voice,
and Israel paid no attention to me.
I sent them away according to the desires of their hearts.
They will walk in their own ways.” And again, it was because of pride and disobedience that the Lord said in anger,
“I brought forth wonders [?] and raised them up,
but they rejected me. An ox knows its owner, and a donkey its master’s feeding trough,
but Israel did not know me, and my people did not discover who I am.” And again, it was because of pride and disobedience that the Lord threatened these people at that time,
saying, “I sent you all my servants, the prophets, by day and early in the morning.
I sent them, and they did not listen to them, nor did their ears pay attention.
Instead, they followed the thoughts of their evil hearts.”
Again, because of pride, Scripture has been indignant with these people from the beginning:
saying, “The sin of their mouth,
“The words of their lips—let them be caught in their pride.
They will declare their end through their curse.” We said these things knowing that, just as the love of money is the root of every evil, according to the words of the Scriptures,
so too disobedience is the root of every evil,

according, again, to the words of the Scriptures, especially among those who harbor hatred toward their neighbors without cause, carrying out their murders in their hearts instead of with their hands.
The Lord spoke with Adam from the beginning, establishing a covenant with him when he created him, placing all creation on earth into his hands and those of his descendants.
And he established an everlasting covenant with him and his descendants, saying, “Be fruitful and multiply, fill the earth and rule over it.
The fear and dread of you will fall upon all the wild animals, all the livestock of the fields, all the birds of the sky, and all the fish of the sea.
I have placed them under your control. They will be food for you; like the green plants, I have given them to you.
But you must not eat raw flesh with its lifeblood.
For I will also demand an accounting for the blood of your lives.”
I will demand an accounting for it from the hand of every wild beast.” Will God, then, judge the wild beasts?
Do beasts really have hands, then, as he said?
“I will demand an accounting for it from the hand of the wild beasts”?
But God knew from the beginning that many people would change into the nature of beasts by allowing the devil to dwell within them and carry out his murders through them,
just as Cain did this before long. As he added to the statement, “Whoever sheds a human being’s blood,
his own blood will be shed in return,” truly in accordance with the words of the Scriptures.
there are many people whom wild beasts surpass in goodness. For wild beasts, this is their nature.
But the people who have changed and acquired the heart of a wild beast—it is not their nature.
Or again, Scripture will tell us that there are many people who outwardly take on a human appearance but inwardly are wild beasts.
Just as the devil takes on the appearance of an angel of light, although he is darkness.
and he is a murderer.
For Paul also wrote about the people of Crete, “They are always liars, evil beasts,
lazy bellies.” He also describes the full extent of the conduct of people who have changed from their own nature into the nature of beasts.
He says, “If, in human terms, I fought with beasts in Ephesus.”
Did the holy apostle really fight with actual beasts in Ephesus?
Rather, they were people who behaved like wild beasts instead of human beings.
The Lord of glory, Jesus, speaking with his holy apostles, says concerning those who have the character of beasts rather than human beings,
“Look, I am sending you out like sheep among wolves.
So be wise like snakes,
and innocent like doves. Beware of people who have the character of beasts rather than human beings,
for they will hand you over to councils and flog you in their synagogues.”
For that breed of beasts will not disappear until the end of the age.
Nor will the blessed breed of sheep in the fold of the good shepherd, Christ, disappear until the end of the age.
Especially those sorts of people who live in idleness, as it is written, “Every idle person is absorbed in desires.”
If Scripture said, “Be still and know that I am God,” it does not give permission for each person to stop working to sustain their life and obtain food and clothing.
Rather, it says, “Refrain from the works of the flesh,” namely sexual immorality, idolatry, sorcery, hostilities, quarrels, jealousies, contentiousness, divisions, factions, and slanders.
like [?] and things of this kind.
If those who engage in these things will not enter the kingdom of heaven,
neither will they understand that God is God, as Scripture said:
“Be still and know that I am God.” For indeed, unless a person stops
or desists from lawless deeds,
he cannot do righteous deeds,
as the Lord said, “No one can serve two masters.
For either he will love one and hate the other, or he will cling to one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon.”
If the Lord also said, while speaking with the Jews at that time, “Do not work for food that will perish, but for food that will last forever,”
the King and the King's Son is not speaking
—God and the Son of God—about food and clothing to prevent a person from working for what he needs, so that we may not impose a burden
or hardship on any of you by having you provide for us from your own possessions. How, then, should it be now?
can anyone say that he can maintain his livelihood securely without working, when the Lord commanded Adam from the beginning, when he placed him in paradise, to work in it and guard it?
For he did not leave him without work or without the duty of keeping the fruits of his labor safe, as it is written.
“With every precaution, guard your heart,
For through these things there are paths of life.
And after he cast him out of paradise, he did not leave him idle, without working.
Rather, he said to him, “You will eat the plants of the field by the sweat of your face,”
and, “You will eat your bread until you return to the earth.” Whom has God ever blamed, from the beginning,
for working for their food and clothing? Rather, from the beginning Scripture speaks in reproach,
saying, “For we hear about some among you who live in an undisciplined way, doing no work at all, but being busybodies.
We therefore command people of this kind, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to work quietly and eat their own bread.” Or again, “Do not let anyone who does not work eat.”
Or who among all the holy people is there whom Scripture does not point out,
And Scripture recounts the work of each one, setting them before us as examples through their work: Cain and Abel, the firstborn. Did not one become a shepherd, while the other worked the land?
God did not blame Abel for tending the sheep,
nor was he angry with Cain for working the land.
Rather, it was Cain's lawlessness that condemned him,
and it was Abel's righteousness that justified him. And again, Noah, to whom the Lord spoke,
saying, “You are the one I have seen to be righteous before me in this generation”—
Scripture testifies about him: “Now Noah was a farmer.”
He began to plant a vineyard.”
Then again, the great Abraham, with whom God made a covenant to multiply his descendants like the stars of heaven,
and like the sand on the seashore, which cannot be counted, and to let his descendants inherit the cities of their enemies,
and to let all the nations receive a blessing through him, as we know, since the Old and the New Covenant came into being through him and his descendants.
And we find it written about him: “Abraham planted a tree [?] beside the Well of the Oath.”
He called that place by the name of the Lord: “God, the Eternal One.” Or was Abraham not a sower
and a reaper? Would he himself have planted beside the Well of the Oath after he had finished making a covenant with Abimelech, as it is written about him?
“Abraham was very rich in livestock, silver, and gold”?
Then did not Lot look up and see that the whole region of the Jordan was well watered, and settle there with his livestock?
because they were numerous?
He was the one whom God rescued from the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, along with his wife and his children.
Or is it not written about Isaac that he sowed in that year?
and obtained a hundred measures of barley?
Then again, Jacob, whom God blessed because of his father Abraham and Isaac—does he not himself say:
“I burn in the heat of the day and in the frost of the night.
Sleep has departed from my eyes.”
“Look, for twenty years up to this day I have tended your sheep”?
Did the Lord withhold his blessing and leave him unblessed? Or did he fail to multiply his descendants because he was always in the fields?
Not only did God bless him, but his angels too were with him among the sheep,
as they appeared to him in the dream: “Lift your eyes and look at the white-faced rams, the spotted ones, and those that are [?],
and the gray-colored, speckled ones mounting the sheep and goats.
For I have seen what Laban is doing to you.”
Indeed, not only were the angels with him among the sheep, but they also traveled with him on the road, guiding him as he went up to Canaan, the land where he was born,
as Jacob looked up and saw the camp of God coming toward him,
and the angels of God met him.
When he saw them, he said, “This is the camp of God.”
And he named that place “The Camp.”
Or who rebuked Laban as he pursued him to lay hands on him,
he and his relatives, saying, “Be careful not to say anything evil to Jacob”?
As Laban said to Jacob when he met him, “You have carried off my children like prisoners taken by the sword.
You did not allow us the honor of kissing my sons and daughters. Now you have acted foolishly.”
“And now I have the power to harm you. But the God of your father said to me yesterday, ‘Be careful not to speak to Jacob
with evil words.’” Likewise, Jacob also spoke to Laban when he argued with him: “Unless the God of my father Abraham had been with me,
and the Fear of Isaac, you would now have sent me away empty-handed.”
But God saw my humiliation and the toil of my hands.
He rebuked you yesterday.”
We have said these things so that we may understand that not only do the angels walk with him, but the Lord too is not far from him, being with him wherever he goes.
Just as he also spoke with him elsewhere, in the same way that he appeared to him as he was coming down to Egypt with him:
“And I will bring you up out again, and Joseph will lay his hand upon your eyes.” Then again, the sons of Jacob,
whose descendants God multiplied like the stars of heaven and like the sand on the seashore, which cannot be counted—
were they not in the countryside tending their father’s sheep? Just as Jacob called Joseph
and sent him, saying, “Go and see whether your brothers and the sheep are well, and bring me news of them,” sending him out from the valley of Hebron.
Now he had come down to Shechem, and a man found him wandering in the fields and asked him, “Who are you looking for?”
He said, “I am looking for my brothers. Tell me where they are tending their flocks.”
He said to him, “For I heard them say, ‘Let us go up to Dothan.’”
We have said these things because God will not disgrace someone for being in the countryside, doing his work for his food and clothing, while pleasing God.
Nor will he honor someone for being shut away as an ascetic, idle and not working with his hands, especially when he does not please God through good works
and good deeds. Rather, the person in the countryside must please God so that God will bless him
and also bless the produce of his land.
It is also right for someone who has committed himself as a monk and an ascetic to work with his hands
with his food and clothing, and do God’s will through acts of piety, so that he may receive a blessing from the Lord upon the earth.
and find mercy before God on the day of his visitation.
For we say these things so that we may understand that God loves everyone who fears him and hopes in his name, and everyone who works with his hands so that he may have
money. And sexual immorality, theft, lying, and false oaths are evident in the person who practices them.
Those near him and those who live with him often find him out or catch him. But the person who hates his neighbor,
or envies his neighbor—they are within the heart and are not apparent to their neighbors and those who live with them.

But just as the devil is hidden, along with his demons of darkness, in what he does out of hatred for the whole human race, so too is the person who envies his neighbor and hates him: his evil deeds are hidden within him.
Both day and night are darkness to him in the chamber of his heart, because his deeds are not apparent.
Because of sin, the Holy Spirit said, knowing that [?].
more than all acts of lawlessness, concerning those who do these things: the person who speaks peaceful words to his neighbor while hostility, envy, and hatred are in his heart.
“Give them according to their deeds and according to the wickedness of their thoughts.
Give them their recompense.” What, then, will he give them? Or what is their recompense? He will lay upon them the curse they loved.
and make it a crown upon their heads.
Of words that [?].
You will tear them down and not rebuild them.
O blessed one! O love for humanity, you are adorned on every side!
the virtues of the Spirit, as you go into Christ’s presence to receive according to their worth in the resting places in heaven.
For their appearance is not a human appearance,
But
the deception of human beings, fraud.
rejoicing over your neighbor’s destruction—but the Scripture of God stands against it.
And the things she said from the beginning about those who do these things, to send her down and scatter her,
like those who do not exist at all. And the time when she will give her spirit into the hands of the one who hates her,
Christ, and all her bitter lamentations, according to what is written: “Whoever rejoices over someone who is being destroyed will not escape harm.”
For indeed, when the Lord became human among human beings—God and the Son of God—

he is the one who commanded Adam in paradise not to eat from the tree. He is the one who commanded Abraham and his household to undergo circumcision of the flesh. He is the one who spoke with Moses at the bush,
having performed all these mighty deeds through his staff, about which he spoke to Moses, saying, “Take this staff in your hand,
the one with which you will perform all these signs.” He went still further in accomplishing them before Pharaoh and all the Egyptians,
by the power of his arm, as it is written: “The one who [?] Israel out of the land of Egypt with a strong hand and an uplifted arm.”
He is the one who gave the law to Moses in the wilderness, and the one through whom every commandment and every law came into being.
He is the one who did these things, having done far, far more than what we have said, for there is no limit to his mighty deeds.
And there is no end to his wonders. So when he became human among human beings, he was God and the Son of God.
An expert in the law approached him.
He questioned him to test him, saying, “What is the greatest commandment in the law?”
The true Savior, Jesus, answered him,
saying, “Listen, Israel: the Lord your God is one.”
You shall love the Lord
your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your thoughts.
and your neighbor as yourself.” He answered him, “Well
you have spoken: God is one, and there is no other besides him.
And, “You shall love him with all your heart and all your strength and with all your understanding.”
“This,” he said, “is better than all burnt offerings and sacrifices.”
And when the Lord of glory recognized that he had honored love for humanity as it deserved, he granted him the kingdom of heaven without hesitation.
“You too are not far from the kingdom of heaven.”
But he wanted to understand the perfection of love for others, so that he would receive greater honor.
He asked him, “Who is my neighbor?” The King of the powers answered him, teaching him about the perfection of the straight path: “A man went out from Jerusalem to Jericho.”
He fell into the hands of some [?] robbers. They stripped him and wounded him.
They went away and left him half dead.
By chance, a priest came down that road.
He saw him and passed him by.
But a Samaritan came down that road, saw him, and had compassion on him.
He approached him and bandaged his wounds.
He poured wine and oil over him and put him on his own animal.
He brought him to an inn and took care of him. The next day, as he was leaving, he gave [?] coins.
To the innkeeper, saying to him, “Take care of him.”
“And whatever you spend on him, I will repay you when I return.” Who among these three
He said, “The one who became a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of the robbers.”
He said to him, “It is the one who acted in spirit [?] toward him.”
The Lord of glory, Jesus, said to him, “Go and do these things yourself as well.”
This is so that we may know that we have said nothing distorted in what we have said outside Scripture, and also so that we may know that love is love for others, and love for others is love.
If he granted this man the kingdom because he spoke the truth in his answer—that love for others is better than all burnt offerings and sacrifices—
then what about the person who himself brings it to perfection within his heart?
and all its other righteous deeds—how greatly will he honor him?
And how will he grant him the kingdom of heaven?
So let us not boast, brothers and sisters, that we are Christians while there is envy, strife, or hatred toward our neighbor in our hearts,
or while we do not love our neighbor as ourselves.
we are not perfect in our deeds.
The name by which we are called is nothing but an empty name.
The holy apostle cries out, “For where there is envy and strife among you, are you not worldly?”
And are you not living according to human ways?”
What, then, will we say on the day of our visitation, if we have not recognized our condition before the days of our lives come to an end?
And we will wail in the place of wailing, where many have wailed since the beginning of the world,
and we will weep in the place of weeping, where many have wept since the beginning.
If it is because of you, O love for others and love, that this whole multitude will receive glory when the King comes in his glory with all his angels, as we said before,
and they will enter eternal life,
then blessed are you, and blessed is the Lord of glory, Jesus, because he has sown you for himself in the hearts of the wise.
so that they may inherit everlasting life, with every honor and all glory, with great confidence in heaven.

And if it is because of you yourself, O hatred of humanity, that this entire multitude and these many peoples, from the beginning of the age until now and until the end of the age, will suffer disgrace,
when the King comes in his glory to judge between these and the others—among those on the right because of love and mercy
and perfect love for humanity, and among those on the left because of envy and hatred and mercilessness—
then cursed is the one who spread you,
the devil having sown you for himself as an evil seed in the hearts of the foolish.
For it is he, the dragon, who fed you with the abundant venom coming from his mouth, until he led very many astray without their realizing that he had led them astray
from the road leading to the city where they dwell, having brought them out of the light into darkness without their realizing that it was darkness.
in which they are walking, according to what is written:
For whoever hates his brother is in darkness and walks in darkness,
not knowing where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes.
until they hear this voice full of wrath coming from the mouth of Jesus the Almighty, as he questions them about what they ought to have done.
according to the decree of judgment written in the Gospels.
This is what he made known to us beforehand—he who does not wish anyone in his creation to perish—saying, “This is how I will act
when I come, according to what those on the right deserve, according to their deeds performed with every kindness toward humanity.”
And again, “This is the [?] allotted to those on the left when he comes, according to what they deserve:
Receive now for yourselves, O miserable, wretched people, together with this one whom you loved and with whom you worked in envy and hatred
and in utter mercilessness, down in the fire of Gehenna—not for days or years, but forever and ever.”
For these things will happen at the end of the age, and there will be no further judgment after this,
and no further day to look forward to for resurrection, after he has judged the angels and passed judgment on the full extent of all lawlessness,
and sends them down to Hades in his furious wrath, whether they are among the angels whom he deceived or among the human beings whom he led astray:
The angels will drive them all away:
everyone defiled by the lawless deeds of the son of destruction, who did not repent before they died or abandon those deeds before the day of their visitation.
Once and for all, without exception, everyone standing on the left will be thrown down into Hades and inherit the fiery Gehenna forever.
Oh, what turmoil there will be on that day for those standing on the left, in the presence of those on the right who are in glory!
Oh, what weeping there will be on that day among all the nations that did not know God,
and all the heretics, each one separately in the error into which the deceiver led them!
But people who say of themselves, “We are Christians,” will be in great wretchedness and great misery on that day,
having failed to recognize the calling with which they were called and the grace that reached them.
especially those who bear the name and wear the garb and live in the holy places,
They too are caught up in these things in that wrath, because they did not listen to the voice of the Scriptures, which went out over the whole earth,
and its life-giving words, which reached the kings of the inhabited world, crying out, “Flee from sexual immorality!”
“Every sin a person commits,” it says, “is outside the body.
But the person who commits sexual immorality sins against their own body.”
Or, “Whoever joins himself to a prostitute is one body with her.”
“But whoever joins himself to the Lord is one spirit with him.” Or, “Do you not know that you are God’s temple and that God’s Spirit lives in you?” Or, “Whoever defiles God’s temple—
God will destroy that person.”
What, then, will happen after the outcry of these people and after the humiliation of those on the left, in great fear, while the ministering angels,
flames of fire, surround them, and the sentence of Jesus the Almighty comes out of his mouth, pursuing them in wrath and terror:
“Depart from me,
you who are cursed, into the everlasting fire prepared for the devil and his angels,
because you did not act according to what I commanded you. It was not merely that you did not love your neighbor because the task seemed difficult to you.
Why, then, did you hate him instead, turning justice into gall and the fruit of righteousness into bitterness?
You exchanged what I told you for things I did not tell you, in every kind of lawlessness.
Now receive what you deserve, according to the wickedness of your deeds, in the fire of Gehenna, together with the one who turned your goodwill into hatred and your love into mercilessness,
and your purity into defilement and sexual immorality in many forms that are disgusting to mention and shameful to hear about.
He is the one who turned complete godliness into every kind of complete ungodliness during the days you were on earth.
You did not listen to me as I cried out through the mouths of my servants,
the prophets, ‘Return to me so that you may live’—these things from the beginning of the earth.
Or, ‘Return to me, and I will heal your wounds.’ Or, ‘Come out from among them and separate yourselves from them,
and I will welcome you, because I am merciful.’ Or, ‘I will be your God, and you will be my people.’
And, ‘I will be your Father, and you will be my sons and daughters.’”
For if the one who is pure and those who are being purified all come from one, according to the Scriptures—that is, from God—
then do not the defiled one, the devil, and those who are defiled likewise all come from one—that is, from him—whether a demon or any of the unclean, deceiving spirits that are with him?
whether prostitutes or men who are worthless in every way, they all come from him, the devil—everyone who sins in any way.
What, then, will happen after the judgment of Jesus the Almighty, and the Son of the Almighty Sabaoth, seated upon the cherubim, has been fully carried out,
with the shining seraphim standing before him, together with the holy archangels, with great glory, and all his saints, as it is written: “The saints are the ones who will judge the world”?
and they drag all those on the left down into Hades with the devil, and shut him in there with them, and shut them in with him?
What remembrance, then, will there be of these people before God from this time onward?
Oh, this great anguish and this great sorrow for anyone who understands what will happen on that day!
For we did not obey the Scriptures, but forgot and cast their words behind us.
We have taken on hardness of heart and negligence until these things overtake us, although we did not want them to overtake us.
And until we find ourselves among these things, although we did not want to be among them. Did the Lord not say,
“Everything you want people to do for you, you yourselves also
must do for them in the same way.
“For this is the Law and the Prophets”?
For the good Savior did not hide the matter from us by failing to tell us, “The gate is wide.”
and the road leading to destruction is spacious.”
Nor did he forget to tell us about the other one, that it is narrow and constricted.
And continuing to affirm the practice of love for humanity, while putting envy and hatred to shame,
he says, “But I tell you: love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.”
so that you may become children of your Father in heaven. For he makes his sun rise upon the good and the evil, and he sends rain upon the righteous and the wrongdoers.
“For if you love those who love you,” he said, “what reward do you have?
Do not the tax collectors themselves do the same? And if you greet only your brothers, what more are you doing than the other Gentiles?”
Do they not do this?
So be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect.”
The holy baptizer John cries out from the beginning, since he said these things,
him ahead of himself to guide the people toward love for humanity and love,
since there is nothing greater than these among all the virtues. When the crowd came out to receive baptism from him, they asked him, “What should we do?”
He told them, “Whoever has two tunics should give one to someone who has none, and whoever has bread should do likewise.”
And the holy apostle, whom the Lord sent to proclaim the gospel,
cries out, saying, “Brotherly love.”
continue.
“Do not neglect hospitality, for through it some have welcomed angels without knowing it.”
What, then, is greater than love for humanity—as we have said many times—and love? For she is exalted beyond measure.
For mercy is her garment, and the fulfillment of the commandments of life
is what serves as a crown on her head, as she greatly terrifies the enemies by going into God's presence.
And the devil always trembles before her, filled with shame in her presence, seeing the likeness of Christ that she wears and the sign of his holy cross.
For it was because of his love for humanity and his mercy toward humankind that he endured the cross.
For, finding fault through the prophet,
he speaks threateningly about this kind of people, whose hearts are full of deceit while they speak pleasantly to their neighbors.
There is indeed wrath before God against those who conduct themselves this way. How far, then, does their judgment reach? It reaches to the depths of Hades.
Since we have spoken about the prophet,
He says in the fury of his anger, as we said earlier, “Look, I myself will refine them.”
Where, then, will he refine them? And let me test them, for I will act in the face of the wickedness of the daughter of my people.
Their tongue is an arrow that strikes.
The words of their mouths are deceitful. They speak peaceful words to their neighbors, while hostility and hatred are in their hearts. “Will I not, because of these things—
—call them to account?” says the Lord. “Or will I not take revenge on a people like this?”
So that we may understand that all the words of Scripture oppose this way of acting from the beginning,
The Old Testament and the New Testament. Now, since we have learned everything—our death and our life, our fullness and our lack, our going into God's presence rightly
by our wisely keeping the things he said, and our descent into the underworld when we foolishly transgress the things he said.
Let us therefore now reflect on these things and the others, before the day comes that we do not know.
and the hour that we do not recognize, and we receive according to our deeds, each one according to what he deserves and according to the fruit of his deeds.
Oh, blessed are those people because of whom God will be glorified through their good deeds, which are the fragrance of Christ!
Oh, woe to those people because of whom their parents’ names will be disgraced through their lack of discipline!
The true and good Savior commands, “Do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing
“Whenever you perform an act of mercy”—and good is the one who said this.
Again, revealing the deeds of a good person elsewhere, he says, “Let them see your good deeds and glorify your Father who is in heaven.”
So, then, there is no way for a person’s good deeds to remain hidden.
For it is like a person who has fragrant aromatic material inside his clothing, though it is not giving off very much scent:
he will not be able to restrain its fragrance and prevent people from smelling the fragrance inside him whenever he passes them.
In the same way, no one who performs good actions and good deeds before God will be able to hide them and prevent people from knowing about them.
Whether it is night or day, he will not be able to hide them, as the Lord said: “There is nothing hidden that will not be revealed.”
Again, it is like a person who has a great stench inside him and gives off a very foul smell, though he does not want to, nor does he wish people to smell him whenever he passes them.
But it is unavoidable because of the overwhelming stench. This is how it is with a person who performs actions
that do not please God and are abominations in people’s sight. Even if he does them at night, in the darkness,
they must be revealed, as the apostle said: “Things that are otherwise cannot remain hidden.”
Strive, therefore, my beloved brothers, and let us accomplish the work for which we have gathered together, namely purification, along with the other commandments entrusted to us by God
through our holy father, so that we may receive honor on earth before both the good and the wicked,
and also be honored still more in heaven before God and all the saints,
and receive the reward for the good deeds we have done on earth, in the heavenly capital, Jerusalem of heaven, [?] every good thing.
For our holy father Apa Athanasius says, “Preserve the honored human image, for they will not call you a human being,” he said, “if you do the deeds of irrational creatures.”
Now then, beloved brothers, dear to the Lord, we have great reason to boast about you everywhere we go, taking pride in you.
as people tell us about your former deeds, saying, “Here is a people who are chosen and adorned
In wisdom, fearing God and also keeping their fathers’ commandments, we hear of no conflict among them,
or any sound of war. Instead, they spread the news of your faith everywhere. Do outsiders live with us, so that they would know what each one of us
is like in his conduct? Rather, they see the [?] around us and its sweet fragrance—the righteousness of our fathers—shining around our congregation,
shining more brightly than the sun and spreading a sweeter fragrance than all spices. Because of this, they honor us all the more and add to our goodness.
If we have done a little, they will proclaim much more, and they tell one another about many good deeds, saying, “We do them.”
Truly, we feel ashamed and become nothing compared with what people outside say about us.
Now then, brothers, let us be firm, like a city whose walls are strong and whose gates are shut.
For the Scriptures have said, “Like a city whose walls have been demolished,
so is a person who does not act with counsel.”
What counsel, then, is Scripture speaking about, except God’s counsel? As it is written,
“There are many thoughts in a person’s heart.”
but it is God's counsel that stands firm.”
“A person is a great thing,” it says, “and a merciful person is precious.”
I too, wretched and poor as I am, will put it this way:
For a person is a great thing, and a holy person is even more exceptional.
Let us therefore carry out the work of godliness in every activity, whether in all our spiritual activities
or in bodily activities through the work of our hands, so that we may receive a blessing from the Lord
and mercy from God our Savior, and that it may be said of us,
“This is the generation of those who seek the Lord.”
Please, then, my beloved brothers, be diligent about the morning reading and the reading at evening, and about your morning and evening gatherings.
Carry them out fully and patiently, without being disturbed by the one who causes trouble. For it is written,
“The one who troubles you will bear the judgment, whoever he is.”
Then the written word will call you blessed: “Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord, the people whom the Lord has chosen as his inheritance.”
And the words of Scripture will again call you blessed all the more: “Blessed are the people who know the shout of joy.
Lord, they will walk in the light of your face, and they will rejoice in your name all day long.”
They will be exalted through your righteousness, for you are the glory of their strength. Our horn will be exalted through your righteousness.
And then you yourselves will also be able to declare confidently, “The Lord is our protector; the Holy One of Israel is our king.”
Oh, blessed are people like us, whom many mouths will call blessed on earth!
and they are also called blessed in heaven by the mouths of tens of thousands upon tens of thousands in the heavens.
Oh, truly, woe to people who follow our way of life in the congregations of God whom those on earth will call blessed!
while those in heaven—vast multitudes—disown them because of their deeds.
Woe to people about whom those on earth say, “They are the ones,” while those in heaven say about them, “They are not the ones.”
Woe to people who live in the houses of God, his congregations and his holy places, about whom those on earth say,
“They are the children of God,” while those in heaven say, “That is not so. Rather, they are children of darkness and enemies of God because of their evil deeds.”
Especially those who actually commit these evil deeds—acts of pollution and defilement—in the houses of Christ. [?] the laypeople on earth,
especially since they will be hidden from those in the heavens, according to what is written:
“What is crooked cannot be set right,” and, “What is missing cannot be included in the count.”
Oh, blessed are people who follow our way of life and trust in their purity, just as our holy father
said this many times in his holy letters.
Woe, woe to people for whom this is not the case and who do not possess this in the congregations of God!
Oh, blessed are people who place their hope in their own hope, knowing that it pleases God and is accepted by Christ because of their wisdom
and their prudence, having acquired for themselves hope in heaven and indescribable wealth forever.
And woe to people who have no hope in heaven and do not know what it is that they trust in,
or what it is. Because of these deeds—these very deeds—and because of their foolishness and disobedience, such people have acquired for themselves misery and poverty,
and everlasting weeping and mourning down in Hades.

Therefore, insofar as we have understood, brothers, what we ought to do during these five days that are quickly passing away, as it is written by another holy man, “For my lifetime has become like a runner,”
let us not forget or be negligent, for we will not be given another day.
When each person's days have come to an end, if we speak, we will have much to say about the misery of those who are negligent.
And again, if we speak, we will have much to say about those who become rich through their diligence,
as they put their work right and heal themselves through repentance after they have fallen. For this task lies before everyone on earth at all times who wishes to be saved.
But it is our own desires and our disobedience that make us unworthy of these things. For it is indeed written:
“Unless the Lord builds a house, those who build it have labored in vain.”
And, “Unless the Lord guards a city, its guard has spent the night keeping watch in vain.”
And again, “No one can say, ‘Jesus is Lord,’ except through the Holy Spirit.”
And again, the Lord of glory, Jesus, says, “Without me you can do nothing.” Therefore, unless God works with a person,
a person cannot work alone for his salvation. For when a person works with God in good actions and good deeds,
God, in turn, works with him through every blessing and makes him grow in the fruits of righteousness.
Who, from the beginning, ever placed his hope in God and was abandoned by God, among those you read about?
It is the same now. He says, “I am he; I am he. And when you grow old, I am still he.” Jesus Christ is the same yesterday,
and he is the same today, and forever.
Oh, blessed are those who understand and recognize the difference between good and evil—evil, on the one hand, so that they may guard themselves against it.
against doing it; but good, so that they may carry it out cheerfully.
It is written,
for, “It is a cheerful giver whom God loves.”
What, then, is a giver? It is not merely someone who gives bread and clothing to his neighbor, but whatever you do among the works of righteousness, completing them joyfully,
whether prayer, ascetic discipline, purity of heart and purity of body—doing all these joyfully—or praising God by day and by night,
So that you may know for whom you do these things, and also know from whom you will receive their reward. He knows.
that whoever approaches God must believe that he exists and that he will reward those who seek him.
So then, let us not neglect ourselves at sowing time, so that we may find something to reap or gather.
Many people toil without understanding [?] how to watch over themselves. The written saying will be fulfilled concerning them: “Why do you toil,
and your labor brings no satisfaction?”
This is how it is: there is nothing new under the sun among the things that have been tested.
have been tested from the beginning,
And they were written for our instruction through those who had been disciplined.
and with whom the Lord spoke.
For I have already said this many times.
it is not just one sin that fights against a person, but very many.
Not only is hatred of people cursed, as has been written about it,
but injustice is even more cursed.
For this reason Scripture says, “Let everyone who speaks the Lord’s name turn away from injustice.”
Likewise, our holy father did not speak idly in his holy letters about slander, saying these things and others:
“Woe to those who join one another in slander, running to one another with a great desire to carry it out together!”
I, this miserable, poor man, put it this way: just as those who run to one another, burning fiercely through the devil’s influence, desire to commit sexual immorality,
so it is with those who run to one another to engage in slander.
Indeed, I have said these things many times because of the harm suffered by people of this kind, who destroy their own hope.
at the same time, and wasting their efforts, with no benefit for them in all their toil because of their mouths and their ears.
Is it not written, “Whoever says, ‘I am a worshiper of God,’ but does not restrain his tongue—this person’s worship is worthless”?
For whoever takes part in slander and gossip takes part in sexual immorality without knowing it. The man who commits sexual immorality and the woman with whom he commits it
keep looking anxiously this way and that, so that people will not see them, until they have carried out their acts of sexual immorality.
The slanderer and the listener also withdraw to one side by themselves, looking this way and that, anxious that people might hear them before they finish their slander.
For this reason, both groups are cursed together by God: those who commit sexual immorality and those who slander.
Indeed, the person who slanders is no different from the person who practices sexual immorality, and the person who practices sexual immorality is no different from the person who slanders.
For just as a person's heart is filled with filth,
and burns with desire for sexual immorality, without any way to carry it out according to his evil desires unless he finds a woman to commit it with,
or else satisfies those desires in other, unnatural ways with people he finds ready to engage in their cursed practices, both these and the others,
so it is also with slander.
Even if an ungodly person's heart is filled with its filth, he cannot carry out his impure acts with his mouth unless he finds someone like himself, under this same curse,
who burns with desire to hear about his neighbor's faults and disgrace.
For the listener will enjoy himself like a prostitute who enjoys the pleasure of those who commit sexual immorality with her.
This is what the person who listens to slander wants: not to have the slanderer get up and leave him,
and not to make him stop insulting his neighbor. What, then, are these two like?
The speaker and the listener are like Satan and lawlessness, and lawlessness and Satan. Or indeed, is the listener not worse than the slanderer?
This is how the listener keeps looking out after the other person has left him, having carried out all his sexual immorality with his mouth into the listener's ears,
like someone who commits sexual immorality, carrying out all his sexual immorality with his mouth into the listener's ears,
like someone who commits sexual immorality, carrying out all his sexual immorality in the embrace of an evil woman, as he keeps looking out in the burning desire of his evil heart,
to see whether someone else is also coming to tell him things, just as the one who got up told him.
so that he may enjoy still more the humiliation of many people who are better than he is. Likewise, the prostitute who displays herself in the streets, becoming a snare for
many miserable people, after this man has left her, having carried out his sexual immorality with her,
looks again for another man or others, looking for people she may find who are like her, under this same curse,
this man and that other one, so that they may commit acts of sexual immorality with her. People like these should have spent the effort they put into such things on pleasing God,
better if people of this kind—the slanderer and the listener—had sought only their own glory and boasted in it,
rather than seeking their neighbors' disgrace and the humiliation of their fellow servants of God,
since it is the same God whom they worship, and the same Lord whom they serve.
rather than enjoying a pleasure full of weeping without knowing it, and rejoicing with a false joy over their neighbors' disgrace—a joy full of grief, though they do not realize it.
What the devil wants is also what these people love, and what the demons rejoice over.
is also what they rejoice in.
For our holy father himself also said this with anger and wrath from God:
"It has been said of two kinds of creatures that they cast their desire into their mouths.
One kind," he said, "is among the birds that are in the waters of the rivers, and the other is among the creeping creatures on the ground."
“This is what this kind of person is like,” he said: “the one who slanders and the one who listens to him.”
What, then, is the portion of these people, or what is the lot of those others?
If all the words of anger in Scripture, which it spoke on God’s behalf, come down upon them—for “I have cast out the slanderer”—
his neighbor secretly,” or, “You sat slandering your brother, and you laid a stumbling block for your mother's son.”
“You did these things, and I kept silent.”
“You thought [?]”
“that I would be like you.”
“I will rebuke you and set them before you. Understand these things, then, you who forget God,” he said.
Recognize your disgrace now from these things, lest he snatch you away and there be no one to rescue you.
“A sacrifice of praise [?] will honor me,” he said—not slander! Certainly not! “This is the road that I will show you, so that I may see God’s salvation.”
Oh, then, what will happen if the words of Scripture stand against us at Christ’s judgment seat? For this is indeed how it will be.
Do you not know, you poor, wretched human being, that what you sow will grow, and what you cast into the ground will come up?
If the good Savior said, “The kingdom of heaven is like
a mustard seed, which a man took and sowed in his field, and which is smaller than all the seeds”—
Then, when it grows, it becomes larger than the vegetables and becomes a large tree, so that the birds of the sky come and dwell beneath its branches.
so, when you sow good fruit in the ground, it produces an abundance of good fruit that is sweet and beneficial to people.
Likewise, when you sow bad fruit in the ground,
it grows up crooked and harms those who pass by. If you sow a seed of the [?] in the ground, does it not grow? Or how does it produce its yield?
It and all the other good and choice trees in the garden—how does their owner enclose them with walls?
He fences them in and watches over their fruit, because they are good to eat and benefit people.
Likewise, the vineyard is guarded because its wine is beneficial
and because it brings joy to those who drink it, especially the sick.
But look, in turn, at the seeds of the thornbush, if you sow them in the ground, along with weeds
and every crooked, wild tree: how they produce their yield without those who tend them enclosing them with walls.
Nor do they look for their fruit, except as fuel for those who burn them, who have no need of their seeds.
Recognize the fruit of those who practice righteousness on earth from what we have said. And recognize, too, the fruit of those who practice lawlessness on earth from what we have said.
Since, then, the devil knows—and he is cunning—
that a human being is victorious on the road by which he will go to his Creator, he therefore does all he can to deceive many of those who will obey him.
Oh, you are cursed, devil, because of these many different seeds that you have cast into your evil heart,

making their odor work as they lie buried in the hearts of the foolish, who hate their own souls, unlike those who love their souls. May it not happen! Until you make them strangers to life, how many will you cast out, and how many will you leave?

But this snare, this one that you prepared for those who bear the name and wear the habit, and who are in the places belonging to Christ, especially throughout the land of those who wish to devote themselves to God—
it is hidden and more troublesome than all your snares, just like idolatry and the heretics.
For you have darkened their hearts until you led them astray and made them blind, so that they would not know the God who created them.
I am speaking of hatred, slander, and jealousy, through which you have secretly [?] among those people.
Scripture cries out, “Whoever slanders his brother or judges his brother slanders the law.”
and judges the law. But if you judge the law, then you are not someone who carries out the law.”
Truly, whoever slanders his neighbor resembles many acts of lawlessness. He resembles the sexually immoral, as we have already said.
And he resembles a thief in what he does. Like the shame of a thief,
when they catch him, according to the words of Scripture, with the stolen goods in his hand—
such, too, is the shame of a slanderer.
And the listener, if the person who is the target of the slander comes upon them, or hears them without their knowing, after they have finished all their wickedness
and the words of jealousy and hatred in their mouths, and they look over to their side—
and see him standing there, listening to them without their knowing it. And let them look behind them and see him in everything they have said.
they did not realize how greatly it changes—
their face—and their heart melts, so that we may understand that the fate of the thief
such is the lot of the slanderer and the listener.
If your face has changed and your heart has melted because the person you are slandering has heard you,
then how distressed will you be, or how much will your face be filled with shame, when those you do not know come for you
and bring you before the one you have never seen, Christ, to repay you according to your deeds—he who loved humanity, who did not curse when he was cursed,
who offered himself up as a holy sacrifice to his Father, not for one or two people, nor for just one nation,
but for the whole world of those who wish to be saved; he who gave us boldness and enabled us to cry out to him at all times.
Recognize what he says to you, O human being, and his love for everyone together,
as he taught us to cry out to him and his Father when he taught us to pray: “Our Father in heaven,
He did not tell you to say only “My Father,” but “Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.
may your kingdom come.
May your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.”
“Our bread for the coming day,” he said.
He did not enable you to say, “Give me today my bread for the coming day,” but, “Give us today our bread for the coming day.”
“Forgive us our debts,” he said.
He did not tell you, “Forgive me what I owe.” He said, “As we too forgive those who owe us.
You are alone in your prayer, but with your mouth you bear witness for many that they forgive those against whom they have something.
And do not bring us into temptation.”
You are one person, yet you pray for many with the words that the Savior, who loves humanity, has put into your mouth.
But rescue us from the evil one, for yours are the power and the glory forever and ever. Amen.
Then recognize the love of Christ, as we said before: he makes his whole creation one in their prayer, wanting us to love one another, whether in our living together or in our conduct,
whether in our going to church or in our partaking of the body and blood of the Lord,
being united in love and of one mind in Christ, praying for one another in love,
as he taught us to pray, so that he may accept our prayer from us, rescue us from the evil one, and freely grant us the kingdom of heaven.
And let us forgive every grievance in our hearts against our neighbor, so that he may forgive us too,
so that we do not become liars in our prayer when we say, “Forgive us, as we too forgive those against whom we have a grievance.”
And again, “If anyone has a grievance against another, just as Christ forgave you,
you too must do the same.” And again, “If you forgive people their sins, your Father in heaven will also forgive you your sins.
For if you do not forgive people their sins,” he said, “your Father will not forgive you your sins.”
What do we now have to do with jealousy, hatred, and slander,
especially impurities, defilements, acts of violence, greed, and all the other abominable deeds of the devil and his demons, when God and his Christ
are uniting us in sonship to him in the kingdom of heaven, so that we may inherit with Christ forever and ever, in all glory and every blessing forever?

What do we now have in common with the devil and his demons, that we should be punished along with him down in Hades, in the fire of Gehenna and with the worm that never sleeps, although we do not belong to him?
He does not come from us now, but we come from God.
For it was he who breathed the breath of life into our face, and we have become one with him through the body and blood of his holy Son,
whom he freely gave us. We have come to share a single sonship with the holy Trinity, whether young or old, male or female—everyone who partakes of the body and blood of the Lord—
We have become one with God,
not as gods—certainly not!
but as a child of their holy Father and as a brother of the blessed Christ, the King of heaven and earth.
in accordance with what he said with his truthful mouth: “Whoever does the will of my Father who is in heaven”—
when they asked him, “Look, your mother and your brothers are standing outside, wanting to speak with you,” and the one speaking to him answered, “Who is my mother?”
“And who are my brothers? For whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and my sister and my mother.”
Since, then, we have these promises, my beloved,
let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of flesh and spirit, bringing our purification to completion in the fear of God the Lord,
as the apostle said, giving no cause for offense in anything, so that no one may find fault with the ministry,
just as he also said this.
Blessed are you, Lord God Almighty,
the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who created everything through his holy, beloved Son.
Blessed are you, Jesus Christ.
And blessed is the Holy Spirit, the Counselor, together with his holy Father, for every blessing upon the earth,
and for all kindness and compassion upon the earth, and for patience and forbearance.
For if you do not forgive us, God Almighty, and if you do not cover our sins, Jesus Christ, we have no standing before you.
Nor will we appear before you at all.
But we beg you, God of hosts, who performed all these wonders in Israel from the beginning for the sake of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
to perform them again for us now, for the sake of your holy name and for the sake of your beloved holy Son, Jesus, our Savior and our life.
Do not hold us to account, because we are flesh, and
we are dust, just as you said from the beginning to the first man, Adam: “You are dust, and you will return to dust.”
Forgive us, because we are clay and the work of your hands. Have compassion on us, God of hosts.
Forgive us, because we are grass, just as you said through your mouth, [?] your prophets: “All flesh is grass.”
You are the God of hosts, through whom all power exists. You are the one who made the earth like nothing, while those who live on it are like locusts before you.
They have been compared to spittle, and [?] a drop hanging from a bucket, and like the tipping of a balance, according to the words of your prophets.
O God of hosts and Lord of glory, Jesus, if you do not have compassion on us, who will have compassion on us? If you do not have mercy on us, who will have mercy on us?
For you know our powerlessness and our weakness, and the frailty of our body is not hidden from you. You are blessed, Lord, and you are holy.
And blessed is the name of your holy glory forever and ever.
John’s Exposition
In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, the Trinity, of one substance and undivided.
We believe in the begetting of the only-begotten Son from his Father before the foundation of the world. We believe in the birth of our Savior from the Virgin Mary, who is a virgin at all times.
We believe in the sufferings that our Savior endured for us on the cross, which is full of salvation.
We believe in his resurrection from the dead.
We believe in his ascension into heaven.
We hope to receive forgiveness of our sins through his holy body and his true blood.
After this canon of Saint Apa John had been lost throughout the whole church, and people had ceased to know that it existed at all,
the Lord gave it to us in a small book written in an ancient hand.
We moved it to serve as a lasting memorial.
We placed it under the authority of our fathers in the desert, so that it would remain under the authority of the church of the Virgin Mary on the mountain, in the days when Father Menas
and my father Zechariah were its stewards, so that everyone seeking this holy canon might receive it from them, find comfort in its words, and return it to them.
so that this great and perfect archimandrite, Apa John, may give thanks for them—for whoever takes care of him—and make him worthy of the resting places in heaven.
And may he write their names in the book of life. Amen. May it be so, may it be [?].
The rich will honor the one who is rich in spirit by stretching out their hands in mercy to the needy, who share this same nature with you.
The poor will honor her who gave birth to the one who willingly became poor for your sake, so that he might make us rich in righteous deeds.
Slaves will honor her who gave birth to the one who emptied himself, taking the form of a slave for your sake,
by showing genuine service to their earthly masters.
But even more, let all of us together show it toward the commandments of our Lord.
We priests will honor her who bore for us the priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek, by purifying ourselves,
as it is written: “Let the priests who approach God purify themselves, lest the Lord destroy some of them.”
We are all the more afraid that we may be found closer to him here than everyone else,
but farther from him there than everyone else because of our sins.
But all of us together, whether priests or the people,
let us plead and pray with all our heart
to her who has greater power than all the saints to plead for us before God: the holy Mother of God, Mary, whom God has honored in heaven and on earth above all creation,
both visible and invisible, so that she may intercede for us before her Son, the true God,
so that he may cover the sins we have committed up to now in the great ocean of his love for humanity,
and remove this heart of stone from us.
a demon, so that they too may inherit the fire and the worm with him.
They are laughing at him now [?] down in Hades—
all those who have gone down to him from the beginning until now, and those who will also go down to him until the end of the age, according to what each person's sins deserve.
What difference, then, is there now between the devil and his demons, and Judas and all the sinners who will die in their sins without repenting, while they themselves laugh at one another
in the fire of Gehenna?
We want to understand that sinners do not laugh at one another—the devil and his demons down in Hades, and the pagans and the heretics,
and the barbarians and the Jews who do not believe in the Lord Jesus—for they are all alike in the fire and the worm that never sleeps.
Look at a place that is very deep and exceedingly wide, and take some of every good tree,
from among all the choice trees of Lebanon.
And every tree that exists on the earth, of every kind, down to thorns and reeds.
And [?] them all, and take some from all of them and throw them into a dry, open place, and set yourself on fire, while a wind
blows fiercely upon them at God's command. You will see that the appearance of their smoke and their burning differs from one another in [?].
For the wise have already understood.
And they have no need of this illustration, for this is what those in Hades are like.
For they are in the midst of [?], in the fire.
And they are beneath the worm that never sleeps. For God created the worm that is in Hades,
and the scorpion,
to be immortal,
just as he also created the unquenchable fire, to punish the devil and his demons down in Hades by means of the fire that never goes out.
Likewise, we learned this through the accounts of the holy martyrs: he spares none of those we have mentioned,
just as we found him punishing them all and condemning them to death through the terms of his decrees, which are written in the accounts of the martyrs.
As it is written in his letters: “Such and such great bishops of the region, if they wish to obey my decree that I have issued
and worship the gods,
they will receive great authority, not only in their city,
but throughout the whole region,
But if they do not obey my decree," he said,
"and do not worship the gods,
they will be condemned to death.” And this is also how the holy martyrs endured until they received the crown of life.
We have said these things because, if the king to whom God has given authority to reign over the earth
has such terror and anger, with a great threat against those who reject his decrees
and oppose his edict, so that he punishes them with swords and many other punishments, as it is written,
“A king's anger is like a lion's roar”—although he teaches godlessness and the destruction of the souls of multitudes—
and has a threat of such magnitude,
and an anger that cannot be appeased with money.
then how much more will the King of heaven and earth, the maker of everything,
the one who created everything out of what did not exist—the heavens and the earth,
the sea and everything in it—not become angry?
Or can anyone restrain his furious anger against any person, whether male or female, small or great, priest or monk, king or ruler, or any leader of the people,
who rejects the Lord's commands and his law, his ordinances and his judgments, and his testimonies, which he testified to us from the beginning through the mouths of his holy prophets
and through the mouth of his holy, only-begotten Son Jesus, as the apostle says: “In many portions and in many ways, God spoke to our ancestors long ago through the prophets.”
But in these last days he has spoken to us through the Son,
whom he appointed heir of everything,
through whom he also made the ages.

And again, through the mouth of his apostles: What, then, will happen to people like these? Or who will be able to endure the fury of the wrath of God, the King of heaven and earth, who teaches true worship, so that people will not worship wood and stones,
as did the kings who ruled, those whose terror and furious wrath we have spoken about,
who also teach people to worship wood and stones and all the other things
made by human hands? But the Lord teaches people to worship him in spirit and truth, because he alone is the true God,
as it is written: “God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship him in spirit and truth.”
And also to serve him, because he is the King of heaven and earth.
And he is the one who created them when they did not exist, whether angels, rulers, authorities, or all those in the heavens, for they all came into being through him.
Look, then, we have understood that woe awaits every human race,
if it does not keep the Lord’s commands given in the holy Scriptures.
As for the kings we have spoken about, those who withdrew from the truth,
punish bodies with the sword,
or rather, with fire and other tortures—but the soul itself they will not be able to overpower.
Nor will they see it.
Nor do they know where it is within a person.
Instead, it leaves in secret and goes into God’s hands, and he gives it what it deserves.
But God himself punishes both the soul and the body of those who disobey him, together in the fire of Gehenna, which is in Hades.
O God, the only true God,
and Lord of glory, Jesus, we have nothing to say before you if you judge us and call us to account
according to what our evil deeds deserve. But you will forgive for the sake of your name alone, because it is holy.
and glorious forever.
Woe to everyone who neglects the truth and remains in sin until death,
just as we have said this many times.
What, then, have those who remain negligent until they die in defilement not lost?

They have lost the angels’ gracious coming to them on the day of their visitation, to greet them with joy and sing hymns with them in a voice of gladness and rejoicing, as it is written: “I remembered these things and poured out my soul within me,
for I am passing through the place of the wondrous tent.”

The place where there will be weeping and grinding of teeth.
We ought to become wise, like all those who have become wise through the many words of the Scriptures, as Scripture has called us to repentance from the beginning.
An animal trained to walk from its youth does not change its way of walking, except through weakness, even into old age.
But we have been taught the deeds that bring us salvation, or the deeds through which we will be saved.
Yet we, for our part, forget them.
Or, even if we were instructed in them at one time, at another time we pay no attention to them.
If the whip is in the hand of the person driving the animal, and it is afraid and walks properly along its path,
then the words of Scripture are even more than a whip for a human being, so that we may listen to them and continue walking in everything according to what pleases God.
Or does Scripture not say, “A whip for a horse,
And a goad is for a donkey, but a whip is for a foolish nation. What is the whip for the foolish nation, if not the words of the Scriptures, as it is written:
“The person who brings wisdom out of his mouth strikes a foolish person with a whip.”
Oh, the great sorrow I am about to speak of! It is a disgrace to us who neglect to listen to God when he calls to us:
“Come out of your sins and come to me by doing a few small good deeds, and I will receive you.
I will become a father to you, and you will become sons and daughters to me, says the Lord Almighty.”
Is the snake not a dangerous wild animal? Yet with a short incantation, when the charmer charms it,
such a wild reptile leaves behind the wildness of its nature and takes on a gentleness contrary to its nature.
It comes out into the hands of the person charming it with great gentleness because of the few words it heard from the charmer’s mouth.
But we, whose hearts have become closed, have not listened to all the words of the Scriptures—those of the Old Testament and those of the New, and those of all the saints,
especially those of our holy father. They all call us to leave behind the sins that are contrary to our nature,
because of which we will die, and to do good deeds in accordance with our nature, because of which we will be saved.
And we have not listened even until now. Instead, we have become like a deaf snake that stops its ears and does not listen to the voice of those who charm it,
or to a charm performed by a wise man, according to the Scriptures.
What must happen before we turn away from our evil deeds?
We commit lawless acts, though we cannot bear the fury of God’s wrath.
We constantly provoke him with our evil deeds, especially we priests and monks who live in the places belonging to Christ.
Oh, how great will be the rebuke we receive on the day of our visitation, if we do not quickly withdraw from these deeds!
As it is written: “The person who does not heal himself through his deeds is the brother of the person who destroys himself.”
“If a fool asks questions,” he said, “it will be counted as wisdom for him.”

Again, wishing to honor those who will abandon their sins and repent quickly, he says, “As for the one who heals himself through his own deeds, the name of the Lord is revealed in the greatness of his power.”
But the righteous will be exalted by running to him, because his love for humanity is revealed toward everyone who will abandon their sins and never return to them from this moment onward.
Or do you not know that it causes great grief before God when people sin in his holy places, especially if they do not quickly abandon their sins?
If God said to Moses at that time, when he spoke with him at the bush, “Take the sandals off your feet, for the place where you are standing is holy ground,”
although it was only a sandal—then how much more will he say to us who live in his holy places,

“Strip yourselves of all these lawless deeds: defilement and pollution, theft and lies, envy and hatred, fighting and rivalry, and all the other sins that are hateful in my sight. For the place where you live is holy ground,
and I dwell in it. My holy name has been proclaimed over it,” just as he said through the prophet,
“Undo every bond of violence and injustice,” so that we will not be left with nothing to say.
For when the commander of the Lord’s army appeared to Joshua near Jericho, he did not hesitate to tell him,
“Take the sandals off your feet, for the place on which you are standing is holy ground.”

This also makes clear what we have said: it is not right for us to remain living in Christ’s places while disobeying his holy law. We must quickly tear apart every bond of lawlessness and cast them off us,
so that the one in heaven will laugh at them,
and the Lord will mock them, speak to them in his anger, and terrify them in his wrath, so that the enemy
and his cursed demons will not continue to hold back or obstruct those who want to leave their sins behind and repent quickly.
so that they may receive a blessing from the Lord and mercy from God our Savior,
And let them say, “This is the generation of those who seek the Lord and who seek the face of the God of Jacob.”
Oh, how great is our reproach!
We are the ones who do not heed all these words until these five days in which we are living slip away from us,
and your lot comes to be with all those who have been disobedient from the beginning. They disregarded the words of those who wanted their salvation and advised them to do good.
They paid no attention to doing it, until they went down to the underworld.
If you do not know your lot, you who will die in your sins, especially in Christ’s places, we will tell you what it is according to all the words of the Scriptures.
Your lot is the lot of Cain, who was the first on earth to receive the curse from God’s mouth because he did not heed his parents’ instruction.
Nor did he strive to imitate the conduct and good deeds of his brother, righteous Abel. Instead, he prepared eternal punishment for himself from God.
In the same way, we too have not heeded the words of the Scriptures
by turning away from our evil deeds and doing good, so that God would have mercy on us.

Nor have we striven to imitate the conduct and good deeds of our righteous brothers with whom we live, until we have prepared for ourselves punishment and everlasting repayment below in the underworld.
You are counted among those whom the Lord swept away in a flood of water at the beginning, because they had pursued evil from their youth.
And the earth was filled with violence because of them, according to the words of Scripture, since they did not listen to righteous Noah as he advised them.
He was the one who built an ark for himself to save his household. Through it he condemned the world and became an heir of the righteousness that comes through faith.

And as for the statement, “Through it he condemned the world,” he did not condemn the world merely because they saw him building the ark, three hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high,
building it piece by piece, with a first, second, and third deck, and coating it inside
and outside with pitch. He was telling them that a flood would come upon the earth, having become a preacher of righteousness, as it is written.
And they did not listen to him until they met a sudden death in wrath at the hands of the one they had angered, God Almighty.
and until this great destruction and annihilation came upon the earth.
There was no son to cover his father’s body and bury him, nor was there a father to cover his children and lay them to rest amid the waters of the rivers,
when the deep burst open and the floodgates of heaven opened. Nor were there wives to cover their husbands,
nor husbands to cover their wives, nor brothers to cover their brothers.
Instead, this same destruction came upon them all at once. Nor did any commemorative offering go up on their behalf to remember them,
or tears and burnt offerings offered in memory of the dead. Instead, they were all swept away in destruction, except Noah alone, who survived with his wife and his children in the ark.
After he came out of the ark, he offered offerings on the altar, and the Lord smelled a pleasing fragrance.
He was pleased and established an everlasting covenant with him.
Likewise, we too have not repented, being [?] those ancient people whom he destroyed before us.
Nor have we emulated our brothers who do good amid hunger and thirst, with many fasts and frequent nights of keeping watch,
in purity—the great subject we are discussing—in renunciation, and in all the good deeds they do,
which bear witness to their love for God, because he himself, the Lord, the good Savior, loved them still more, even to the point of death,
death on a cross. They do these things and others, while we watch them and live with them,
yet we have not repented.
Nor have we listened to the warning that an end is coming, no different from the waters of the flood—I am speaking of death.
Just as the ancient giants and all the people who perished were not granted the sight of Noah
and his entire household who were saved, so sinful people and lawless brothers will not be granted the sight of righteous brothers in their rest
and their joy, when they die in their wickedness.

because they disobeyed God.
